correctness.rationale: The substitution \(R=e^{-s/k}\), \(\lambda=m/k\) transforms the published sharp-root equation exactly into \(p\tanh(\lambda s/2)=2/(e^{2s}-1)\). Opposite strict monotonicity gives uniqueness. The large-ratio limit follows directly; the small-ratio argument proves first \(s\to\infty\) and then \(\lambda s\to0\), which validates the Lambert-W asymptotic. The balanced-ray formula follows from an exact quadratic in \(R^{2k}\). Representative numerical roots were checked only as a sanity test.
